target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: obovoid FLOPO:0991025 to cylindrical PATO_0001873)
reason: A shape between two existing values, like 'linear-lanceolate'; the continuum pattern relates obovoid (FLOPO:0991025) and cylindrical (PATO_0001873).
French/Spanish paniculiforme = panicle-like, said of inflorescences.

The axis forks into two apparently equal branches, as in the earlier rule dichotomous = bifurcated; the different origin (a sympodium or dichasium, not a true apical fork) is not kept, so a new term for 4 statements is not justified.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: rhomboid PATO_0001938 to orbicular PATO_0001934)
reason: A compound of two plane shapes; the examples read 'rhombic-orbicular to r...', a continuum between rhomboid and orbicular.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: lanceolate PATO_0001877, approximate per docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md, to elliptic PATO_0000947)
reason: A compound of two values in which 'sub-' marks the first as approximate; this is the continuum pattern plus the approximate-value qualifier, not a term.
Same meaning as multistemmed, whose synonyms already include multi-stemmed.
A rippled surface or wall is wavy; PATO undulate has the synonyms wavy and waved and covers a rippled surface, as noted in the earlier review for sinuate.

label: dichasial
definition: A branched quality inhering in a cymose inflorescence by virtue of two opposite lateral branches arising below each terminal flower.
reason: French 'cyme bipare' = dichasium. PO has dichasium only as a synonym of several inflorescence classes, and pleiochasial FLOPO:0991327 exists without its two-branched sibling; FNA candidates also use 'dichasial'.
French 'bréviaxe' (of a nut or drupe) = shorter along the base-to-apex axis than broad, which is the definition of depressed.
'One-seeded' is a count of seeds in the fruit, not a quality of the fruit.
French 'à base droite' could mean a straight (truncate) base or a symmetric (not oblique) base, and the bearer is an unspecified 'scale'; too ambiguous for a rule.
'Presque nul / casi nulo' = almost absent or extremely reduced (pedicels, style, septa); the approximation stays in the record and must not become a firm absence in OWL.

A verb relating the part to what it bears (scales, leaves); the content is the presence of the borne part, which is grounded from that part, not from 'bearing'. Rejected like 'covered' in the earlier review.
French 'crépu' = crisped or frizzled; it describes the finely curled ridges of an orchid labellum callus. Crisped has the synonym crispate.

target: docs/odp/18-position-of-the-bearer.md (branch PO_0025073 has position basal FLOPO:0991002)
reason: 'Low branching' / 'bas branchu' says where the branches arise on the trunk, i.e. the position of the branches, not a branching quality of the plant.
French médifixe / Spanish mediifija = anther attached at its middle; the class exists.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (two qualities of the margin: membranous FLOPO:0991046 and fringed PATO_0040008)
reason: Two co-occurring qualities of the bract margin (texture and edge shape), not a continuum and not a single value; each gets its own annotation.
Minutely toothed margin; PATO dentated (synonym toothed) is the nearest existing term, and the size prefix does not justify a new term for 4 statements.
Covered with minute prickles, which is the definition of muricate (many minute, hard, pointed outgrowths).
A transcriber's field name, not a quality word; the examples mix theca position, exsertion and insertion on the filament.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (right angle to PATO_0001321 towards the axis)
reason: PATO right angle to is relational; 'at right angle to the rachis/axis' needs the second part. Statements without it should be rejected like the other bare comparisons.

target: docs/odp/06-specimen-condition.md (brown PATO_0000952, on drying or exposure)
reason: 'Brunissant sur le sec / à l'air', 'overripe fruits browning': a colour that comes with a condition or change, so it is brown plus a condition or transition, not a new quality.

target: docs/odp/18-position-of-the-bearer.md (tepal PO_0009033 has position outer FLOPO:0991379; width measurement)
reason: A measurement field of the outer tepals, wrongly placed on the flower; it is the position pattern plus a width, not a quality word.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: strap-shaped PATO_0002430 to lanceolate PATO_0001877)
reason: A compound of two shapes; ligulate is already ruled to strap-shaped.
'Shoots multinodal' = shoots with many nodes, an indefinite count of nodes.
Negation of the existing stipitate value (fruit, staminal column).
Palmately veined = three or more primary veins radiating from one point, which is actinodromous. A prefixed number ('8-palmatinervias') adds a vein count by pattern 03.
A part (the sterile pistil of a male flower), not a quality; 'pistillode absent' is then pattern 15.
Corolla lobes 's'épanouissant à plat' = spreading fully, in one plane; spreading is the existing value and 'flat' only stresses the degree.
Trigonous with a degree word; 'strongly' stays in the record as a qualifier.
